label: Blackburn is reported to claim a special competence-supervenience advantage for non-cognitivism
paraphrase: As Van Roojen reports the argument, Blackburn claims that non-cognitivism particularly explains why respect for moral supervenience is conceptually required even without an analytic inference from nonmoral descriptions to moral evaluations: the practical purposes of moral discourse supply the explanation. This records a disputed comparative claim, not its truth, nor a claim of moral-fact grounding.
